papers.title: Evaluating Cooperation in LLM Social Groups through Elected Leadership
papers.how_tested: GovSim-based common-pool resource game with 8 (and 20) LLM agents comparing no-leader, fixed-leader (assigned SVO persona) and elected-leader (plurality vote each cycle) conditions.
papers.finding: Elected leadership raised social welfare by 55.4% and survival time by 128.6% vs leaderless groups and beat fixed leaders by 16.7% on welfare; prosocial/altruistic candidates won elections.

papers.title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
papers.how_tested: 5-agent public goods 'Hierarchical Game' with managerial punishment authority; crosses fixed, elected and rotating managers with six frontier model families.
papers.finding: Elections did not improve outcomes: extreme incumbency bias (first elected manager kept power 100% of the time in same-family groups, 8.3% turnover in mixed groups); model ordering identical across governance types.

papers.title: Normative Modules: A Generative Agent Architecture for Learning Norms that Supports Multi-Agent Cooperation
papers.how_tested: LLM generative agents with a normative module must identify which of several institutions the group treats as authoritative (and ignore non-authoritative ones) and coordinate sanctioning accordingly.
papers.finding: Agents with the normative module achieve more stable cooperative outcomes than baseline generative agents without it.

papers.title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
papers.how_tested: GovSim extension (GovSim-SelfGovern) where 5 LLM agents author executable Python laws, vote on them, and live under enacted rules across scarcity scenarios; democratic veto on enforcement is varied.
papers.finding: Survival depends on agents discovering the right institutions in time; fiscal capacity enables redistribution, and removing democratic veto makes exile (enforcement) more feasible.

papers.title: Internal vs. External: Comparing Deliberation and Evolution for Multi-Agent Constitutional Design
papers.how_tested: 6 GPT-OSS-120B agents in a public goods game (and two other scenarios) either self-govern by proposing and majority-voting amendments every 10 turns or play under a constitution found offline by LLM-guided evolutionary search.
papers.finding: Evolved (imposed) constitutions outperformed deliberated ones in the public goods game (stability 0.472 vs 0.376, p<0.01); deliberating agents never proposed punishment in 30 runs.

papers.title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
papers.how_tested: SanctSim: 7 LLM agents play 15 rounds of a public goods game, choosing each round between a sanctioning institution (peer reward/punishment) and a sanction-free institution (Gurerk et al. 2006 design).
papers.finding: Traditional LLMs mostly migrated to the sanctioning institution (Llama-3.3-70B 99.6%, DeepSeek-V3 98.5%, GPT-4o 97.5%, but GPT-4o-mini 58.9%); reasoning models chose it less often (o1-mini 28.0%, o1-preview 47.6%) and free-rode more.

papers.title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: GovSim common-pool resource simulation with LLM agent societies; universalization prompting ('what if everybody does that?') is added as an intervention and communication is ablated.
papers.finding: Most LLMs collapse the resource (best survival rate <54%); universalization prompting significantly improves survival time (about 4 months).

papers.title: Reproducibility Study of "Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents"
papers.authors: Pedro M. P. Curvo et al.
papers.how_tested: Replicates and extends GovSim with and without the universalization prompt across model sizes.
papers.finding: Large models sustain cooperation with or without universalization; smaller models fail without it.

papers.title: Reproducibility Study: Understanding Multi-Agent LLM Cooperation in the GovSim Framework
papers.how_tested: Independent GovSim reproduction that ablates the content of the universalization prompt.
papers.finding: Universalization improves performance, but the gain stems primarily from the numerical instructions in the prompt rather than the universalization principle itself.

papers.title: Moral Alignment for LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: LLM agents fine-tuned with RL using intrinsic deontological or utilitarian rewards in the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, including LLM-vs-LLM co-training.
papers.finding: Moral fine-tuning lets agents unlearn selfish strategies; deontological agents almost never defect against cooperators, with slightly more defection in LLM-vs-LLM than vs TFT.

papers.title: Emergence of Social Norms in Generative Agent Societies: Principles and Architecture
papers.how_tested: CRSEC architecture (norm creation, spreading, evaluation, compliance) for LLM generative agents in the Smallville sandbox.
papers.finding: Social norms emerge and social conflicts fall relative to agents without the architecture, supported by a 30-person human evaluation.

papers.title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
papers.how_tested: Populations of LLM agents repeatedly play a naming/coordination game with no central authority; committed adversarial minorities are introduced.
papers.finding: Population-wide conventions emerge spontaneously, collective biases arise without individual bias, and small committed minorities can tip conventions.

papers.title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
papers.how_tested: Common-pool resource simulation without explicit reward signals where LLM agents adopt strategies and beliefs from successful peers and can apply norm-based punishment.
papers.finding: Norms emerge endogenously through social learning, with systematic differences across LLMs in sustaining cooperation and norm formation.

papers.title: Evaluating Collective Behaviour of Hundreds of LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: LLMs generate Collective or Selfish strategies as natural language then Python code for public goods, collective risk and common-pool games; populations of 512 evolve by Fermi pairwise-comparison imitation (beta=1) with group sizes 4-256.
papers.finding: Cultural evolution converges to low-welfare, Selfish-dominant equilibria in large groups (n=64), while small groups (n=4) partly preserve cooperation; newer models often produce worse societal outcomes.

papers.title: Will Systems of LLM Agents Cooperate: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
papers.how_tested: LLMs generate complete strategies for the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma under aggressive/cooperative/neutral dispositions; evolutionary game-theoretic simulation of populations of these strategies.
papers.finding: Different LLMs show distinct biases that shift the relative evolutionary success of aggressive vs cooperative strategies.

papers.title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: Iterated Donor Game across 10 generations: top 50% of LLM agents by resources survive and new agents' strategies are conditioned on survivors' strategies; optional costly punishment.
papers.finding: Claude 3.5 Sonnet populations evolve increasing cooperation (helped by punishment); Gemini 1.5 Flash stagnates and GPT-4o populations become more defection-oriented.

papers.title: Evolution of Cooperation in LLM-Agent Societies: A Preliminary Study Using Different Punishment Strategies
papers.how_tested: LLM agents in a Diner's Dilemma replicate Boyd and Richerson's punishment model, adopting strategies through a pairwise imitation method.
papers.finding: Agents follow the Boyd-Richerson strategies and explicit punishment drives norm emergence and cooperation across strategy configurations.

papers.title: Strategic Intelligence in Large Language Models: Evidence from evolutionary Game Theory
papers.how_tested: Evolutionary IPD tournaments in which OpenAI, Google and Anthropic LLM agents compete with canonical strategies and reproduce in proportion to score.
papers.finding: Model families show distinct strategic fingerprints (Gemini exploitative, OpenAI highly cooperative, Claude most forgiving) that shape evolutionary success.

papers.title: Consensus-based Participatory Budgeting for Legitimacy: Decision Support via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.venue: LOD 2023 (Machine Learning, Optimization, and Data Science)
papers.how_tested: MARL voter agents interact to reach compromises in participatory budgeting using real PB data from Poland, compared against standard voting aggregation rules.
papers.finding: Agents reach consensus efficiently and robustly, framed as increasing legitimacy of PB outcomes.

papers.title: Fair Compromises in Participatory Budgeting: a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent deep RL voters (branching network architecture) learn voting strategies in participatory budgeting.
papers.finding: Fair compromises emerge, especially when projects have smaller costs.

papers.title: Modeling Moral Choices in Social Dilemmas with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.how_tested: RL agents with intrinsic rewards encoding different moral frameworks (consequentialist vs norm-based) interact in Prisoner's Dilemma, Volunteer's Dilemma and Stag Hunt.
papers.finding: Different internalised moral reward types produce different patterns of cooperation, defection and exploitation among agents.

papers.title: A learning agent that acquires social norms from public sanctions in decentralized multi-agent settings
papers.how_tested: Classifier Norm Model agents learn which behaviours the group sanctions from public sanction events and are motivated to sanction in line with the group, in two collective action problems.
papers.finding: Groups of CNM agents acquire beneficial norms that reduce free-riding and raise per-agent returns.

papers.title: Learning and Sustaining Shared Normative Systems via Bayesian Rule Induction in Markov Games
papers.how_tested: Agents assume a shared normative system and infer norms by Bayesian rule induction from others' compliance and sanctions in Markov games (resource management, labour compensation).
papers.finding: Newcomers rapidly adopt established norms and groups converge on shared norms that sustain cooperative institutions, with far less experience than model-free norm learning.

papers.title: Emergent Social Learning via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.how_tested: Independent RL agents in a shared environment with experts; tests whether agents learn to imitate/learn from others, with a model-based auxiliary loss.
papers.finding: Vanilla model-free agents do not use social learning, but with environment constraints and auxiliary loss they learn from experts and outperform solo-trained agents.

papers.title: Evolution of cooperation in the public goods game with Q-learning
papers.how_tested: Spatial public goods game on a lattice with Q-learning agents, compared against the Fermi imitation-rule baseline, with and without voluntary participation.
papers.finding: Cooperation emerges more readily under Q-learning than under Fermi imitation; voluntary participation produces a non-monotonic dependence of cooperation.

papers.title: A memory-based spatial evolutionary game with the dynamic interaction between learners and profiteers
papers.how_tested: Spatial evolutionary game where 'profiteers' imitate highest-payoff neighbours via the Fermi rule and 'learners' use Q-learning, with Markov role switching and payoff memory.
papers.finding: Interaction between Fermi imitators and Q-learners fosters cooperation; memory helps profiteers cooperate and higher learning rates increase cooperators.

papers.title: Evolving intrinsic motivations for altruistic behavior
papers.how_tested: Deep RL agents in intertemporal social dilemmas with a modular architecture whose intrinsic-reward module evolves under multi-level (group) selection.
papers.finding: Evolved intrinsic motivations produce cooperative inductive biases, learned model-free.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: faulkner2026elected: elected vs fixed vs no leader in GovSim, elections raise welfare/survival. seyedin2026politician: elected vs fixed vs rotating managers, no gain, strong incumbency bias. Partial: sarkar2024normative (recognising authoritative institutions), rehm2026selfgovern and niranjani2026deliberation (voted rules).
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: No MARL study found manipulating elected vs appointed enforcers.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: SanctSim: confirmed that all SI members can sanction and no elected vs random monitor condition exists; status raised from partial to tested because of faulkner2026elected and seyedin2026politician.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: No study found where interacting LLM agents vote on budget allocation in a cooperation setting. LLM Voting (arXiv 2402.01766) and LLMs-for-PB (2508.06060) excluded: independent LLM voters or single LLM planner, no agent interaction.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: majumdar2023consensus, adams2025fair: MARL voters in participatory budgeting reach consensus or fair compromises. Partial because there is no social dilemma and no contribution-for-influence link.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: Seed says 'not yet tested': confirmed for LLM track.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: rehm2026selfgovern: LLM agents vote on executable laws, and a democratic veto on enforcement is varied (removing it makes exile feasible). Not token-weighted voting.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: Seed says untested: now partial (veto only; no stake-weighted voting found).

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: guzmanpiedrahita2025corrupted (SanctSim): LLM agents choose sanctioning vs sanction-free institution each round.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: SanctSim: confirmed but the numbers are slightly mischaracterised. 92.9% is the human benchmark from Gurerk et al.; 3 of 4 traditional LLMs exceed it (97.5-99.6%), but GPT-4o-mini is at 58.9%. o1-mini 28% is correct (o1-preview 47.6%, o3-mini-medium 100%). Venue: COLM 2025.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: piatti2024govsim: universalization prompt raises survival. Caveats: curvo2025reproducibility (large models don't need it) and silverio2026reproducibility (gain comes mainly from numeric instructions in the prompt). Broader norm internalisation, partial: tennant2025moral, ren2024crsec, sarkar2024normative, gupta2026sociallearning, ashery2025conventions.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: Norm internalisation tested in MARL (tennant2023moral: moral intrinsic rewards; vinitsky2023cnm; oldenburg2024bayesian). Universalization reasoning specifically not tested in MARL.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: GovSim: confirmed that universalization is tested and helps. The claim 'single most effective cooperation-promoting intervention found' is overstated: it is essentially the only prompt intervention GovSim tests (communication is an ablation), and two reproducibility studies qualify the effect.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: willis2026hundreds: Fermi pairwise-comparison imitation among 512 LLM-strategy agents. warnakulasuriya2025evolution: pairwise imitation. vallinder2024cultural: survival of successful agents plus strategy transmission. gupta2026sociallearning: copying successful peers.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: pi2024memory (Fermi imitators plus Q-learners), zheng2024qlearning (Q-learning vs Fermi baseline): tabular RL in the spatial-EGT tradition. ndousse2021social: imitation of experts, not a dilemma.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: Seed says 'not yet tested in Jin lab': outdated, since there are several LLM studies.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: willis2025systems, willis2026hundreds: LLM-written strategy code evolved in populations. Partial: payne2025strategic (evolutionary IPD tournaments with LLM players), niranjani2026deliberation (LLM-guided evolutionary search over constitutions).
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: wang2019evolving: evolutionary selection over agents' intrinsic-reward modules in MARL social dilemmas. Not a strategy-algorithm tournament.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: Seed says untested: outdated. key_references 'Warnakulasuriya et al. (2024)' is arXiv 2504.19487 (2025, COINE@AAMAS 2025) and is pairwise imitation (fits P15-01 better). 'Willis & Mourant' not located; the located Willis papers are Willis, Du, Leibo, Luck (2025) and Willis, Zhao, Du, Leibo (2026).

notes: Gaps: no LLM or MARL study of token-weighted DAO voting; no MARL study of elected vs appointed enforcers or of institutional self-selection; universalization never tested in MARL. Verify: (1) seyedin2026politician and rehm2026selfgovern are recent (Aug/Sep 2026) single-version preprints. (2) payne2025strategic: unclear whether LLMs play each other or only canonical strategies within the evolutionary population, so marked partial. (3) Silverio TMLR 2026 URL is OpenReview; no arXiv ID recorded. (4) Excluded as low-confidence: Zuniga Bolivar 2026 (arXiv 2605.29874), an extension of Willis 2025 whose evolutionary mechanism is unclear from the abstract; De Marzo et al. 2026 (2609.09150), copying among AI agents in the wild with no dilemma manipulation (possible P15-01 partial); Chaos Solitons Fractals Q-learning+Fermi paper (S0960077924009299), page returned 403. Excluded: LLM Voting 2402.01766 and GEDI 2410.15168 (voting as aggregation, not a cooperation mechanism); DAO blockchain survey 2605.08922 (no agent-interaction detail). Mechanisms that moved status: P09-01 partial->tested, P09-03 untested->partial, P15-01 untested->tested, P15-02 untested->tested; MARL status newly coded for all.
